chapter: Trombonists and bandleaders across the river
title: Celestin's society band versus Dixieland
summary: Celestin ran a 10-14 piece society band playing country clubs, not Dixieland until late in life.

story.theme_name: Who was in the band: naming sidemen and personnel

blocks.x: Well I know, I'm more sure Mr. Bill Harrison knows. You see if I ask him. Yeah I try to see him. Cause all them fellas used to play together. You know what I mean? They know you see. He knows, I know he knows. And uh, yeah you see Buddy Johnson, Yank and uh, well you see Buddy Jones they had more of a musical band big time. Yeah, that's what I thought. Yeah you know what I mean? Society band like Celestine had. You see Celestine had a society band itself you see. Till the way out last he went into that Dixieland, he was a Dixieland band. But he never had no Dixieland band before.
No cause he had something around what, 10, 12 or 14.

Big band. Had songs and everything in it. Oh yeah. No trumpet and trombones, you know what I mean? Songs like that you know. But there never was no, he had a good band. He had a good musical band all right now. But the trouble is, you know what I mean, there wasn't no Dixieland. No Dixieland. Cause he used to have good jobs you know. He'd play all them big time country clubs you know.
Yeah, play like, one place he'd play all the summer, one place he'd play all the winter. For Trent Sheeners and all them people like that you know. You wanna come in? Come on.
